_about: Real consumer commission rulings on health insurance claims, taken only from facts stated in the cited reports. detail_level 'news_summary' means only a short summary was available: verify against the order. Amounts awarded exclude interest. Add more cases with: python -m app.precedents.import_cases <file.csv|file.json>

cases.title: Darshan Kumar vs New India Assurance Company Limited and others
cases.forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Ferozepur
cases.date_note: Order date not stated; reported 23 Aug 2023
cases.policy_type: Group mediclaim (New India Flexi Floater), sum insured Rs 3,50,000
cases.reason_text: Hospitalisation was under 24 hours (clause 3.14.1) and the intravitreal injection was not on the day-care list
cases.summary: A claim for an eye treatment (intravitreal injection) was rejected because the stay was under 24 hours and the treatment was not on the day-care list. The commission ordered Rs 22,536 with 6% interest plus Rs 5,000.
cases.reasoning: Advances in medical care mean some patients are treated quickly without prolonged admission, so genuine claims cannot be denied only for lack of formal 24-hour admission. The policy did not explicitly exclude the treatment.

cases.title: Alluri Venkata Rama Raju vs Aditya Birla Capital and Anr.
cases.forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, East Godavari
cases.policy_type: Active Assure Diamond health plan, cover Rs 10,00,000
cases.reason_text: Non-disclosure of hypertension (citing Section 45 of the Insurance Act); the claim was first treated as withdrawn
cases.summary: The insurer first treated the claim as withdrawn and later said hypertension was not disclosed. The commission ordered Rs 1,00,888 with 6% interest plus Rs 10,000 costs.
cases.reasoning: The policyholder had disclosed his pre-existing conditions and paid a 20% extra premium for them. The insurer's shifting explanations were inconsistent and it offered no convincing evidence of concealment.

cases.title: Naseera Abdul Hameed vs Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd.
cases.forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Kannur
cases.reason_text: Alleged non-disclosure of pituitary macroadenoma (acromegaly), said to have been treated for three years before the policy
cases.summary: A Rs 7,02,420 hospital bill was rejected for alleged non-disclosure of a pre-existing condition. The commission ordered the full bill with 4% interest, Rs 25,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 costs.
cases.reasoning: A disease must be clinically diagnosed and confirmed by competent medical professionals to count as pre-existing. Acromegaly was diagnosed and treated only after the two-year period from the proposal date, so the insurer's argument failed.

cases.title: B.S. Sathya Kumar and Ors. vs HDFC Ergo Health Insurance Ltd and Ors.
cases.forum: Additional District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-III, Bangalore Urban
cases.summary: About Rs 5.9 lakh of hospital bills were rejected for undisclosed diabetes. The commission ordered Rs 5,99,272 plus Rs 20,000 for mental agony and Rs 10,000 costs.
cases.reasoning: The insurer did not document any earlier hospitalisation or treatment for the alleged pre-existing condition, so the discharge summary alone did not prove suppression.

cases.title: Complainant vs United India Insurance Company Limited (title not reported)
cases.forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Delhi
cases.date_note: Order date not stated; reported 11 Oct 2024
cases.reason_text: The period of hospitalisation was less than 24 hours
cases.summary: A medical claim was denied because the stay was under 24 hours. The commission ordered Rs 5,000 compensation for mental agony and harassment (the report does not state the claim payment).
cases.reasoning: The bench noted that medical advances have substantially shortened hospital stays.

cases.title: Sujata Sanjay Patole v. Max Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.
cases.forum: Suburban Mumbai District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
cases.policy_type: Health Companion (cashless), sum insured Rs 5 lakh
cases.reason_text: 24-month specific waiting period for pancreatitis and stones in the biliary and urinary systems
cases.summary: Bills of Rs 6,09,851 at two hospitals were repudiated under a 24-month specific waiting period. The complaint was partly allowed: Rs 5 lakh (the sum insured) with 6% interest, Rs 50,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 costs.
cases.reasoning: The waiting-period clause targeted documented pre-existing pancreatitis and could not be applied to a first-time, life-threatening condition. Making the family pay under a cashless assurance and then repudiating was an unfair trade practice.

cases.title: Madhu Sawhney vs Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd.
cases.forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-VIII, New Delhi
cases.date_note: Order dated 24 September (year not stated); claim rejected 25 Apr 2024
cases.policy_type: Two Platinum health policies (Rs 10 lakh and Rs 25 lakh)
cases.summary: A Rs 3.87 lakh claim was rejected for non-submission of documents. The commission ordered Rs 3.87 lakh with 6% interest, Rs 50,000 compensation and Rs 35,000 litigation costs.
cases.reasoning: Insurers may ask for relevant documents but cannot repeatedly demand material already supplied, or documents not reasonably obtainable, leaving claims pending indefinitely. The hospital had corrected an erroneous kidney-disease entry and the treating doctor confirmed it.

cases.title: Religare Health Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Mr. Subhash Chand Gupta
cases.forum: Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
cases.date_note: Order date not stated; reported 28 Apr 2026
cases.reason_text: Alleged concealment of COPD and dyspnoea on exertion at the proposal stage
cases.summary: The insurer's appeal was dismissed and the district order upheld: Rs 74,219 plus Rs 25,000 compensation for wrongful repudiation.
cases.reasoning: The records showed only tentative symptoms or history, and later tests did not confirm the conditions. The burden of proving concealment was on the insurer, which had medically examined the insured before issuing the policy.

cases.title: Sh. Naresh Kumar Chabba vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd. and Anr.
cases.forum: Himachal Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
cases.policy_type: Mediclaim (Arogya Raksha Plan-B), sum assured Rs 5 lakh
cases.reason_text: First-year exclusion for bilateral knee osteoarthritis (knee replacement) and a 48-month pre-existing disease exclusion
cases.summary: A claim for the wife's bilateral knee replacement was rejected under a first-year condition and the pre-existing disease exclusion. The commission ordered Rs 3,71,436 with 9% interest, Rs 40,000 compensation and Rs 30,000 costs.
cases.reasoning: The first-year condition did not apply to this policy because its special conditions carve out an exception for group health policies, and the insurer gave no evidence of a pre-existing disease.

cases.title: Policyholder vs Star Health and Allied Insurance (NCDRC, reported early 2024)
cases.insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance (as reported)
cases.reason_text: Wrong date of birth and suppression of pre-existing ailments in the proposal form
cases.summary: The NCDRC upheld the insurer's repudiation of a health claim.
cases.reasoning: Where material facts such as pre-existing ailments are suppressed in the proposal, the insurer is within its rights to repudiate the claim.

cases.title: 78-year-old policyholder vs Niva Bupa Health Insurance (NCDRC)
cases.reason_text: Unilateral cancellation of the policy and refusal to honour the claim
cases.summary: The NCDRC declined to disturb a State Commission ruling ordering Rs 9.2 lakh mediclaim and Rs 82,000 compensation to a 78-year-old policyholder.
cases.reasoning: The insurer's unilateral cancellation of the policy and refusal to honour the claim were held unjustified.

cases.title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Smt. Shanta Devi & Ors.
cases.forum: Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
cases.date_note: Reported in the LiveLaw consumer round-up, 23-29 Dec 2024
cases.reason_text: Claim rejected because the treatment was bariatric surgery for morbid obesity
cases.summary: The State Commission held the insurer liable after it rejected a claim for bariatric surgery for morbid obesity.
cases.reasoning: Rejecting the claim because of the bariatric surgery was held improper.
